q: 1. When the curve is to be set out over a rough ground, the method used is ...............
explain: On rough ground where chaining is difficult, methods that use angles or optical distance measurement (two-theodolite or tacheometric) are preferred.

q: 2. The theodolite method off setting out a curve involves ...............
explain: Theodolite methods (like the two-theodolite method) primarily rely on angular observations to define points on the curve.

q: 3. A curve of varying radius is known as ...............
explain: A transition curve is designed to have a radius that changes continuously (usually from infinity to a fixed radius) to provide a gradual change in centrifugal force.

q: 4. In a reverse curve, the super elevation provided at the point of reverse curvature is ...............
options: dependent on the element of reverse curve
explain: At the point of reverse curvature, the direction of curvature changes; therefore, the super-elevation must pass through zero as it switches sides.

q: 5. Different grades are joined together by ...............
explain: A vertical curve is used to provide a smooth transition between two different gradients (grades) on a road or railway.

q: 6. The properties of autogenous curve for automobiles are given by
explain: Bernoulli's lemniscate is considered the ideal transition curve for highways where the deflection angle is large, as it mimics the natural path of a vehicle's steering.

q: 7. The spiral angle of a transition curve will be given by the equation
explain: The spiral (deflection) angle of a transition curve at any point is given by the formula phi = L2/(2*R*Ls) which, at the end of a full transition curve of length L, reduces to the standard form L2/2R (for the total spiral length).

q: 8. Rankine's deflection angle in minutes is obtained by multiplying the length of the chord by .............
options: square of the degree of the curve
inverse of the degree of the curve
explain: Rankine's method relates the deflection angle directly to the chord length and the degree of the curve (or radius).

q: 9. Shift of a curve, is .............
explain: The shift (S) required for a transition curve is calculated using the formula S = L²/24R.

q: 10. A reverse curve consists of
options: a single curve of a circle connecting two straights
two arcs of different radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal or different radii bending in the opposite directions
explain: A reverse curve is composed of two circular arcs (of equal or different radii) that curve in opposite directions, joined at a common tangent point.

q: 11. When the centers of the arcs lie on the opposite sides of the common tangent at the junction of the two curves, it is known as a
explain: This specific geometric arrangement, where the centres of curvature of the two joined arcs lie on opposite sides of their common tangent, defines a reverse curve.

q: 12. The angle between the back tangent and forward tangent of a curve is known as
explain: The angle subtended at the centre of the curve between the back tangent and the forward tangent (or equivalently between the two radii to the tangent points) is called the central angle.

q: 13. The angle by which the forward tangent deflects from the back tangent of a curve is called
explain: The deflection angle is, by definition, the angle by which the forward tangent direction deflects from the direction of the back tangent.

q: 14. The length of peg interval for flat curves is
explain: For flat (large radius) curves, pegs are usually set out at the full standard chord interval of 30 m, as used for the degree-of-curve definition.

q: 15. Different grades are jointed together by
explain: Vertical curves are used to smoothly join two different longitudinal gradients (grades) on a road or railway alignment.

q: 16. The angle of intersection of a curve is the angle between
explain: As stated in Q12, the angle of intersection of a curve is the angle between the (prolongation of) back tangent and the forward tangent.

q: 17. Designation of a curve is made by .............
options: angle subtended by a chord of any length
angle subtended by an arc of specified length
explain: In engineering practice, a curve is primarily designated either by its Radius (R) or by its Degree of Curvature (D).

q: 18. If D is the degree of the curve of radius R, the exact length of its specified chord, is
options: radius of the curve × sine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × sine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × cosine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × tangent of half the degree
explain: Using trigonometry, the chord length $L = 2R sin(D/2)$. Since $2R$ is the diameter, the expression is diameter $	imes sin(D/2)$.

q: 19. The shape of vertical curve generally provided is
explain: Parabolic curves are preferred for vertical curves because they provide a constant rate of change of grade, leading to a smoother transition.

q: 20. Overturning of vehicles on a curve can be avoided by using
explain: 0) A **transition curve** (spiral) gradually changes the radius from infinity to a fixed value, allowing the centrifugal force to build up slowly and providing space to apply super-elevation, which prevents overturning. 1) Vertical curves handle changes in slope (up/down), not lateral stability. 2) and 3) These are types of circular curves that still have an abrupt change in curvature at the tangent point, which is where overturning risk is highest.

q: 21. When R is radius (m) and D is degree of curve, relation for 30 m chord is
explain: For a 30m chord, $R = (30 \times 180) / (\pi \times D) \approx 1718.87 / D$. This is usually rounded to $1720/D$ in many textbooks.

q: 22. In a lemniscate curve, the angle between the tangent at the end of the polar ray and the tangent at the commencement of the curve (i.e., straight) is ............. the angle between the polar ray and the straight .............
explain: In a lemniscate curve, the polar deflection angle ($\alpha$) is related to the total deflection angle ($\delta$) such that $\delta = 3\alpha$.

q: 23. A reverse curve consists of .............
options: a single curve of a circle connecting two straights
two arcs of different radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal or different radii bending in the opposite direction
explain: A reverse curve (S-curve) consists of two circular arcs with centers on opposite sides of a common tangent.

q: 24. The angle by which the forward tangent deflects from the back tangent of a curve is known as .............
explain: The deflection angle is the angle at which the new direction (forward tangent) deviates from the extension of the previous direction (back tangent).

q: 25. The perpendicular offset from a tangent to the junction of transition curve and circular curve is equal to .............
explain: This offset value is mathematically derived for a spiral transition curve to ensure a smooth change in curvature; it is often noted as $Y = L^2 / (24R)$.

q: 26. If the radius of a simple curve is 600 m, the maximum length of the chord for calculating offsets, is taken .............
explain: Using the $R/20$ rule of thumb for chord lengths, $600/20 = 30$ meters is the appropriate interval for calculation.

q: 27. A ideal vertical curve to join two gradients, is .............
explain: A simple parabola is used for vertical curves because it provides a constant rate of change of grade, ensuring smooth vehicle motion.
